mining100-straight-body:
Mining 100: early game progression

Fast path
1. Equip a Muck Bag in a backpack slot.
2. Mine rock or ore with a pickaxe. IME creates muck instead of normal drops.
3. Break a muck pile to move one layer into an equipped Muck Bag. A Muck Shovel collects one layer from each nearby muck pile in a 3 by 3 area.
4. Build a Sieve. Put muck above the Sieve; outputs spawn below it. Sieving metal ore muck is very inefficient. Use it for emergency first nuggets, mineral ores, sand, gravel, and stone output.
5. Build Stick Sluice Baffles in flowing water for early passive ore capture. Upgrade to Sluice Baffles when you have planks and nails.
6. The Screen is not part of the sluice. It is a splitter. Put raw muck above the Screen; coarse muck comes out the front and fine muck drops below. Put coarse muck above a powered Jaw Crusher; fine or raw muck drops below the Jaw Crusher. Send fine and raw ore muck to water and baffles, or save it for smelting.
7. Build a smelting furnace around a Smeltery Door. Sneak-right-click the door to show the structure projection and cycle tier. Put Smelt Pot or Small Smelt Pot blocks in the pot positions shown by the projection. Put ore muck in the pots, add flux, fuel every fuel position shown by the projection, close the furnace, and make sure the fuel is hot enough for the metal.

Smelting furnace checklist
- Pot contents: ore muck. Avoid stone muck; it is wasted during firing.
- Flux amount: 1 flux item per 4 muck layers, rounded up. 16 layers need 4 flux. 32 layers need 8 flux.
- Fuel: every fuel position must be burning. The furnace uses the lowest fuel temperature.
- Timing: 8 hour hold, plus 1, 2, or 4 hours to heat and cool depending on tier.
- Better yield: roast ore muck first in a furnace built around a Roasting Furnace Door.
mining101-straight-body:
Mining 101: straight to the point

What creates muck
Mine rock, cracked rock, or ore with a pickaxe. IME turns those drops into muck. Blasting can also create muck from rock and ore. If the config option Only ore blocks create muck is enabled, normal rock drops stones instead.

Layer counts
- Rock: 5 to 7 stone muck layers.
- Cracked rock: 3 to 5 stone muck layers.
- Poor ore: 1 ore layer and 4 to 6 stone muck layers.
- Medium ore: 2 ore layers and 3 to 5 stone muck layers.
- Rich ore: 3 ore layers and 2 to 4 stone muck layers.
- Bountiful ore: 4 ore layers and 1 to 3 stone muck layers.
- Ungraded ore and mineral ore: usually about 1 to 4 ore layers and 1 to 3 stone muck layers.

Ore muck values
- Concentration: 25 metal units per ore layer by default.
- Coarse ore muck availability: 0.15.
- Raw ore muck availability: 0.25.
- Fine ore muck availability: 0.35.
- Stone muck: no ore content.

Storage
- One visible muck pile stores up to 8 layers. Columns can stack.
- A Muck Bin stores muck and spills its contents when broken.
- A Muck Bag must be in a backpack slot to collect muck.
mining102-straight-body:
Mining 102: straight to the point

Sieve
- Put muck, sand, or gravel above the Sieve.
- Keep space below the Sieve for output items.
- Metal ore muck is very inefficient in the Sieve. With default values, raw and fine metal ore muck usually give 1 nugget per layer, and coarse metal ore muck gives 0 nuggets per layer.
- Use the Sieve for early emergency nuggets, mineral ores, sand, gravel, and stone products.

Screen
The Screen is a separator, not a sluice part. It prepares muck before water capture, crushing, or smelting.
- Put muck above the Screen.
- The front output receives coarse muck.
- The bottom output receives fine muck.
- Raw muck splits into 75% coarse and 25% fine.
- Coarse muck passes to the front.
- Fine muck passes below.
- Both output positions need room, or the Screen waits.

Jaw Crusher
The Jaw Crusher only processes coarse muck and needs IME power.
- Power it through Power Input and Power Connector blocks.
- Put coarse muck above the Jaw Crusher.
- Keep space below it for output.
- Output is 75% fine muck and 25% raw muck.
- Send raw muck back through a Screen. Send fine and raw ore muck to water and baffles, or to smelting.

Water and baffles
- Flowing water slowly moves submerged muck downstream.
- Sluice Baffles capture raw or fine ore muck only.
- Fine ore muck capture chance: 60%.
- Raw ore muck capture chance: 35%.
- Coarse muck and stone muck are ignored by Sluice Baffles.
- Stick Sluice Baffles use half the capture chance and half the storage of Sluice Baffles.

Powered transport
- Power Input: converts vanilla mechanical power to IME power.
- Power Connector: links IME power networks.
- Flat Conveyor: moves muck forward.
- Split Conveyor: routes muck left or right.
- Bucket Lift Body: extends a bucket lift downward.
- Bucket Lift Output: takes muck from the bottom of the lift and outputs it at the top.
mining103-straight-body:
Mining 103: straight to the point

Roasting furnace
A roasting furnace improves ore availability before smelting or blooming. The furnace is controlled by a Roasting Furnace Door.
- Sneak-right-click the door to show the structure projection and cycle tier.
- Put muck in the projected roasting positions inside the furnace.
- Put fuel in every projected fuel position.
- Close the door.
- Required temperature: at least 600C.
- Hold time: 8 hours.
- Heat and cool time: 1, 2, or 4 hours by tier.
- Non-iron ore muck gains +0.35 availability, capped at 1.0.
- Iron ore muck becomes 0.65 coarse, 0.85 raw, or 1.0 fine.
- Each ore layer can only be roasted once.

Smelting furnace
A smelting furnace turns non-iron ore muck into pig metal. The furnace is controlled by a Smeltery Door.
- Sneak-right-click the door to show the structure projection and cycle tier.
- Build the bricks and empty spaces exactly as projected.
- Pot positions are the projected chamber positions: tier 1 has 1 pot position, tier 2 has 4, and tier 3 has 9 on the grates.
- Fuel positions are the projected fuel pockets beside or around the pot chamber. Every fuel position must be burning.
- Use Smelt Pot blocks for 32 muck layers, or Small Smelt Pot blocks for 16 muck layers.
- Put ore muck in the pots. Stone muck is wasted space and is removed during firing.
- Add flux to the pots. Use 1 flux item per 4 muck layers, rounded up.
- Close the furnace and use fuel hot enough to melt the target metal. The furnace temperature is the lowest temperature among its fuel positions.
- Hold time is 8 hours. Heat and cool time is 1, 2, or 4 hours by tier.

Flux and additive values
- Borax powder: +0.10 availability.
- Lime: +0.10 availability.
- Crushed quartz: +0.10 availability.
- Charcoal powder: +0.08 availability.
- Potash: +0.06 availability.
- Charcoal: +0.05 availability.
- Flint powder: +0.03 availability.
- Iron oxide powder: +0.03 availability.
- Total additive bonus is capped at 0.75.

Bloomery
A bloomery processes iron-bearing ore muck. The furnace is controlled by a Bloomery Door.
- Valid vanilla iron ores: limonite, hematite, and magnetite. Geology Additions pyrite also works when that mod is present.
- Fill the projected interior muck positions with iron-bearing muck.
- Drop charcoal or coke into the top/fuel positions.
- Ignite the Bloomery Door with a torch.
- Charcoal gives 1 fuel unit. Coke gives 2 fuel units.
- Required fuel units: muck layers divided by 2, 4, or 6 by tier, rounded up.
- Hold time: 12, 16, or 24 hours by tier.
- Completion places an Iron Mass.
- Breaking an Iron Mass drops 1 iron bloom per 100 iron units and 1 iron bit per 5 leftover units.
mining104-straight-body:
Mining 104: straight to the point

Drilling basics
Drilling sets up controlled blasting through rock and ore.
- Use a drill on the target face with a hammer in the off hand.
- Each drilling increment adds 1 block of depth by default.
- Clean the hole before loading it.
- Load blasting powder, plug the hole, add fuse, then ignite.

Depth ranges
- Starter drill: up to 4 blocks.
- Hand drill: 4 to 8 blocks.
- Long hand drill: 8 to 12 blocks.
- Allowed vertical angles: -90 to 90 degrees in 15 degree steps.

Blasting powder behavior
- Blast radius: 0.75 blocks.
- Microblast spacing: every 0.5 blocks along the drilled path.
- Default dud chance: 0.02.
- Default hangfire chance: 0.04.
- Default hard-fail chance: 0.01.
- Default gas-cut chance: 0.5.
- Default sympathetic detonation chance: 0.5.

Result
Blasting follows the same muck rules as pickaxe mining. Rock and ore that normally create muck will create muck when blasted. If Only ore blocks create muck is enabled, ordinary rock does not create muck when blasted.
